Subject: Please reopen: PR #812 changed the default wavelength frame

I did read the changelog. I have now traced the offset to a default change in PR #812, not to my wavelength calibration.

In 2.5.0, LineList.__init__ changed its default from wave_frame='air' to wave_frame='vacuum'. My optical spectra are wavelength-calibrated in air using arc lamps. With the same input spectra and config, the new default therefore introduces a mismatch between the data and the rest wavelengths. Around H-alpha, the vacuum/air wavelength ratio is approximately 1.00028, consistent with the redshift shift of about 0.00028 I reported, or roughly 83 km/s. Downgrading restores the previous results; explicitly setting the frame also fixes it for me.

For anyone finding this thread with air-calibrated spectra, the workaround is:

LineList(..., wave_frame='air')

Set the frame to match your actual wavelength calibration; this is not a recommendation to use 'air' for every dataset.

The changelog entry says “Refactor LineList and spectral frame handling (#812).” That does not tell users that a scientifically consequential default changed, and there was no deprecation warning. Reading that entry would not have told me to update my configuration.

I am frustrated that this was dismissed as “almost certainly” my calibration or config and marked solved without establishing the cause. I spent two days investigating my calibration and unnecessarily re-reducing arc lamps for 40 spectra. The instruction to “do basic checks” was particularly unhelpful when I had already reported a controlled comparison between versions.

“Works fine for me” does not test this specific case unless the wavelength frame is established. Already-vacuum data, or a radio use case, would not necessarily expose this optical air/vacuum mismatch. m_okonkwo also reported a possible offset in this thread, which warranted investigation rather than closure.

Please reopen the thread and add an explicit note to CHANGES.md describing the default change and migration step. A warning when wave_frame is omitted would also help prevent other users from losing time to the same issue.
